Final for Publication

Application Number: 23123T1

SUBSTITUTE NARRATIVE AND PLANS FOR TYPE 1 ZONING AMENDMENT FOR
940-942 WEST ERIE STREET, CHICAGO
AKA 660-662 NORTH MILWAUKEE AVENUE, CHICAGO

The subject property is a Transit Served Location, as it is situated within 1,000° from the CTA
Blue Line station at Chicago Ave., as well as along the Milwaukee Bus Corridor. It is currently
improved with an older 3-story commercial building. The Applicant intends to demolish the
existing building and redevelop this property with a new 7-story residential building with 48
dwelling units and 24 parking spaces located in the garage; with a rooftop deck to be located on
the principal building. The Applicant needs a zoning change to a DR-S Downtown Residential
District with optional variation relief for rear setback reduction and for elimination of one loading
berth, to allow residential use at the property and to comply with the standards and the bulk
requirements of the Ordinance for this redevelopment project.

Project Zoning Change from an M1-3 Limited Manufacturing/Business Park
Description: District to a DR-5 Downtown Residential District

Use: Residential Building with 48 Dwelling Units and 24 parking spaces.
Lot Area: 10,700 SF (recorded measurements)

Floor Area Ratio: | 4.8

Floor Area: 51,166 SF (see plans attached)

Density: 222 Square Feet per DU

Off- Street Parking: | Parking spaces: 24

Setbacks: South Front Yard: 10 inches
West Side Yard: 2 feet 2 inches / East Side Yard: 1 inch
Rear: 8 11/16 inches (see variation request below)
Open Space (common): 3,363 SF


Final for Publication

Building Height: | 83’-8” per the attached plans

L The applicant will comply with Section 17-4-0301 Specific Criteria for Transit-Served
Locations, should such provisions be determined as applicable:

17-4-0301 Specific Criteria for Transit-Served Locations. In D districts, any new construction
within 2,640 feet of aCTA or METRA rail station entrance or exit must satisfy all of the
following specific criteria:

1. The project complies with the applicable standards of Section 17-10-0102-B Transit-Served
Locations:

The subject property is a Transit Served Location, as it is located along the Milwaukee Bus
Corridor, and it is also located approximately 1,000 feet from the Chicago Avenue CTA Blue Line
Train Station.

2. The project complies with the standards and regulations of Section 17-4-0504, except paragraph E
if the project is not located along a pedestrian street and except paragraph C if the land use is
designated in a non-commercial use group, pertaining to pedestrian streets and pedestrian retail
streets, even if the project is not located along a pedestrian street or a pedestrian retail street;

The subject property is not located along Pedestrian Street or Pedestrian Retail Street; however,
the project complies with the following criteria:

(a) The entire building facade abuts the sidewalk or is located within 5 feet of the sidewalk.

(b) The requirements of Section 17-4-0504-C Transparency standards do not apply to the subject
development as proposed building is entirely residential (non-commercial use group) and there is
no commercial space which would require clear, non-reflective windows, and also the project will
not provide any product display windows.

(c) The building will have a primary entrance door facing Erie Street.

(d) All off-street parking spaces will be located inside the principal building and will not be
visible from the right-of-way.

(e) The parking area will be located inside the building: in the basement and on the ground floor;
vehicle access to the parking area will come via the two proposed driveways, per site plan
attached.

3. The project complies with the general goals set forth in the Transit Friendly Development Guide:
Station Area Typology, and any other station-specific plans, designs or guidelines adopted by the
Chicago Plan Commission.

This Criteria is not applicable to this project.

Final for Publication

4. Residential building projects shall not have a number of parking spaces in excess of 50% of the
Minimum Automobile Parking Ratio for the applicable district listed in Section 17-10-0208 with
any fractional result rounded up to the next higher whole number, unless additional parking spaces
are approved as an administrative adjustment under the provisions of Section 17-13-1003-EE; and

with this proposed redevelopment, the Applicant is proposing a parking ratio which is not in
excess of 50% of the Minimum Automobile Parking Ratio for the applicable district listed in
Section 17-10-0208.

5. The project complies with the Trave] Demand Study and Management Plan rules of the Chicago
Department of Transportation. The City's Commissioner of Transportation is authorized to issue
Travel Demand Study and Management Plan rules consistent with this section.

This Criteria is not applicable to this project.

I. Optional Relief for Adjustment and Variation under Section 17-13-0303-D —

a Type 1 map amendment pursuant to Section 17-13-0300, may include relief available
pursuant to Section 17-13-1000 or 17-13-1100; in such instances, City Council approval of a
Type-1 application containing said elements shall preclude subsequent review otherwise
required pursuant to Sections 17-13-1000 or 17-13-1100, provided that no Type 1
application permits issued may be in violation of Section 17-13-0310:

(A) _ The Applicant also seeks relief for variation under section 17-13-1101-B, from rear
setback requirements of Section 17-4-0406-B, which states that the minimum rear setback
for principal buildings other than detached houses is 30% of lot depth or 50 feet,
whichever is less. The required rear setback for principal buildings other than detached
houses, such as the proposed, applies only to those portions of a building that are 18 feet
or more above grade.

To mitigate site planning hardships on this irregular and substandard lot, the Applicant
requests a reduction in the required rear setback from 24 feet required to 8 11/16 inches
proposed; and to line up with the existing improvements on this short block, if needed,
reduction in the south front setback to 10 inches proposed.

(B) The Applicant also seeks relief for variation under Section 17-13-1101-D, from the
loading requirements of Section 17-10-1101, to reduce the required number of loading
berth from one to zero.

(C) | The Applicant is seeking all relief necessary, as allowed by the Zoning Ordinance, for
the proposed development per the attached Type 1 Plans.

In support of this request, the Applicant states the following:

1. Strict compliance with the regulations and standards of this Zoning Ordinance would
create practical difficulties and hardships for the subject property, since the subject
property is a trapezoid irregular lot with substandard depth between 9’ and 80’, as
compared to the standard lot in the City which has a depth of 125’.

2. The requested variations are consistent with the stated purpose and intent of this Zoning
Ordinance since this proposed redevelopment and corresponding variations are compatible
